moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain the process of organizing and managing tests effectively using the Test Library and Shared Steps Library to improve reusability and efficiency.
Describe how to track changes with Revisions to maintain control over test versions and ensure accuracy.
Articulate how to create and manage Test Plans for web applications to streamline and structure your testing process.
Use Test Suites to group and execute tests efficiently, and use Auto Improve/Smart Locators and Bug Reporting to improve test reliability and collaboration.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Test Library: folders, labels, and test status

elements.description: Folders (create via + → New Folder) give tests a single-location home in the Test Library. Labels are applied/removed via Edit Labels (or right-click → Edit Labels) and, unlike folders, a test can carry several at once — better suited to cross-cutting groupings like 'smoke' or 'checkout'. Search the library with label:<name> to filter by a label.

The documented lifecycle statuses are Draft, Active, Evaluating and Quarantine; Failed is a run result. The status feature is professional-plan functionality and documents CLI 3.135.0 or later. At feature enablement, tests run within the preceding 30 days are identified as Active; this does not promise perpetual rolling automatic promotion. Evaluating failures do not fail CI/Scheduler; quarantined tests normally do not run, with an explicit CLI bypass available.

bulletPoints: Folders = single-location; Labels = multi-tag, searchable via label:<name>.
Real test statuses: Draft, Active, Evaluating, Quarantine — NOT 'Failed' or 'Archived'.
Feature enablement identifies recently run tests as Active; manage statuses deliberately afterward.

elements.description: Clicking Advanced filters opens the Filter Shared Steps pane, letting you filter by step category (Groups, Actions, Validations, Wait for) — the same filtering pattern used elsewhere in Testim's library views, including surfacing steps that are otherwise hidden from the default view so they can be selected and unhidden.

Saving a changed test stores the previous version as a revision with author/date and an optional message. Reverting shared content can affect other instances; inspect the shared references before restoring. A save with no change is not a promise of a new revision.

bulletPoints: Shared Steps Library: Advanced filters → filter by Groups / Actions / Validations / Wait for (including finding hidden steps to unhide).
Saving changed tests creates revisions; inspect shared-content impact before reverting.

elements.description: A web plan selects labels/suites, optional Before All/After All tests and run configuration. Before/after phases use parallel level 1; a failing Before All stops the main list. After All is documented to run when main-list tests fail, but that does not certify successful cleanup after every abort/infrastructure failure. CI invokes the plan through the supported CLI workflow.

Suites collect tests and set an intended order. Parallel execution does not guarantee that order. CLI/Scheduler can run suites; suite creation alone does not provision a CI pipeline or delete unused tests.

bulletPoints: Plans organize setup, main tests and teardown; validate failure behavior and configuration.
Suites collect and order tests; parallel execution does not preserve guaranteed sequence.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Locators: Auto Improve and Smart Locator confidence

elements.description: The documentation describes an Auto Improve attempt below 70% locator score, with replacement and a revision after successful improvement. It applies automatically to writable master, can be enabled on read-only master, and does not run on other branches. Manual locator editing disables future Auto Improve for that locator. An attempt is not guaranteed repair or outcome correctness.

elements.term: Smart Locator confidence and changed attributes
elements.description: Changed attributes may reduce confidence while other weighted attributes still permit matching. A documented page-change warning is associated with a variation greater than 20% from the recorded confidence. Verify the actual target and asserted result; confidence alone does not establish correctness.

bulletPoints: Auto Improve depends on branch/settings and manual-edit scope; success is not guaranteed.
Changed attributes can still match; review confidence warnings and business assertions.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Bug Reporting with the Testim Extension

elements.description: The Chrome extension offers Capture Video & Bug Scenario with screen recording and per-step screenshots. Publishing requires a connected tracker. Bug Reporting also supports reporting a tagged test failure; not all reporting requires a new video capture.

bulletPoints: Bug capture (video + screenshots) is a Testim Chrome Extension feature.
Installing the extension is the first, required step — before enabling any capture settings or connecting a bug tracker template.

examPitfalls.title: Treating 'Failed' or 'Archived' as Testim test statuses
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a test's lifecycle status can be set to 'Failed' or 'Archived' in the Test Library.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented lifecycle choices, distinguishing Failed run results. Check status entitlement and CLI support; Quarantine normally skips execution but has an explicit bypass.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to manually trigger a revision
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Looking for a button to explicitly 'create a revision' before making a change.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Save a changed test to create the revision automatically. Before reverting shared content, inspect affected instances.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Test Suite order is always guaranteed
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Relying on a Test Suite's configured order while also running it with --parallel.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Order is only guaranteed for non-parallel Test Suite runs — passing --parallel means the run order is no longer guaranteed.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to capture a bug video without the Testim extension installed
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Looking for video-capture bug reporting inside the web-based editor alone.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Capture Video & Bug Scenario is a Testim Chrome Extension feature — install the extension first; it's the prerequisite, not an optional add-on.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO names are not among the documented Draft/Active/Evaluating/Quarantine test lifecycle choices?

options.text: Draft
Evaluating
Active
Failed
Archived

practiceQuiz.hint: The real statuses are Draft, Active, Evaluating, and Quarantine.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented lifecycle choices are Draft, Active, Evaluating and Quarantine. Failed describes a run outcome; Archived is not in that documented lifecycle list.

optionExplanations.A: Draft is a documented lifecycle choice, so do not select it.
optionExplanations.B: Evaluating is a documented lifecycle choice.
optionExplanations.C: Active is a documented lifecycle choice.
optionExplanations.D: Failed is a run outcome, not one of the listed lifecycle choices.
optionExplanations.E: Archived is not in the documented lifecycle list.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must you do to unhide a Shared Step in Testim?

options.text: Use the advanced filter to show hidden steps, then select the step and unhide it
Edit the step's properties and remove the hidden flag
Search for the step and select "Unhide" from the dropdown menu
Re-add the step to the test case from the hidden list

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same Advanced filters entry point used elsewhere in the Shared Steps Library.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Advanced filters pane is Testim's standard mechanism for surfacing items that aren't shown by default — including hidden shared steps — so you can select one and unhide it, rather than editing raw properties, a dropdown 'Unhide' command, or re-adding from a separate hidden list.

optionExplanations.A: Show hidden items with the filter, select the item and unhide it.
optionExplanations.B: The documented library workflow uses the filter and unhide action.
optionExplanations.C: Name searching alone does not make hidden items visible in the default list.
optionExplanations.D: Adding another instance does not unhide the shared-library item.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can you integrate a test plan with a CI tool in Testim?

options.text: Test plans cannot be integrated with CI tools.
Select the test plan and run it on the local machine.
Configure the CI pipeline to invoke the supported Testim CLI test-plan workflow.
Manually copy test cases to the CI tool environment.

practiceQuiz.hint: Selecting a CI name alone does not configure a working pipeline.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A CI job can invoke the Testim CLI with the required plan, credentials and environment. Merely selecting a CI tool, running locally or copying cases does not configure that integration.

optionExplanations.A: The supported CLI can invoke plans from CI.
optionExplanations.B: A local run alone does not configure CI integration.
optionExplanations.C: A CI pipeline invokes the supported plan runner with the needed environment.
optionExplanations.D: Manual copying does not establish the configured plan workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can a user create a revision?

options.text: Save a changed test; the previous version is stored automatically.
The user can toggle the revisions button while saving a test to create
A revision will be created every time the user closes Testim
User's can use a previously saved test from their local drive

practiceQuiz.hint: No manual action is needed — it happens on save.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Every time a changed test is saved, the prior version is automatically stored as a revision — there's no manual toggle, no revision tied to closing the app, and no local-drive file involved.

optionExplanations.A: Saving a changed test automatically preserves the prior version.
optionExplanations.B: No manual revision toggle is required for the documented save workflow.
optionExplanations.C: Closing without saving is not the changed-test revision trigger.
optionExplanations.D: A local-drive copy is not this revision mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are the collection and ordering capabilities of a Test Suite, before separately configuring its runner?

options.text: Organizing tests into collections.
Running multiple tests in sequence.
Deleting unused tests automatically.
Automatically provisioning a working CI pipeline and its credentials.

practiceQuiz.hint: The two core benefits are about grouping and ordering, not deletion or CI execution.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Suites group tests and define their intended order; parallel runs need separate consideration. They do not delete tests or automatically provision CI integration.

optionExplanations.B: They define intended sequence; parallel execution can change ordering.
optionExplanations.C: Suites do not delete unused tests automatically.
optionExplanations.D: Runner configuration and credentials are not automatically provisioned by a suite.

practiceQuiz.scenario: On writable master with Auto Improve eligible and no manual locator edit, what does Testim attempt when a locator score falls below the documented 70% threshold?

options.text: The test will fail immediately.
Testim automatically attempts to improve the locator to enhance test stability.
The test will skip the element with the low locator score.
The locator will be deleted from the test.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the Locators: Auto Improve mechanism, triggered below a specific score.
practiceQuiz.rationale: For eligible runs, Testim attempts improvement and records a revision after a successful replacement. Branch/settings/manual-edit restrictions matter; the attempt does not guarantee repair.

optionExplanations.A: Low confidence does not imply immediate failure of every eligible run.
optionExplanations.B: An eligible locator can undergo an improvement attempt.
optionExplanations.C: The feature attempts identification repair rather than automatically skipping targets.
optionExplanations.D: Successful improvement replaces the degraded locator, not deleting the target step.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What happens when the attributes of an element are changed during a test run?

options.text: The test will automatically fail.
The test may pass, but the confidence score may decrease.
The test will become more stable.
The test will skip the changed element..

practiceQuiz.hint: A change does not necessarily prevent a match; inspect actual target and outcome.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Smart Locators weight many attributes per element, so a test can still pass when some attributes change — using the remaining unchanged attributes — but the confidence score for that locator may decrease. It doesn't automatically fail, become more stable, or skip the element outright.

optionExplanations.A: Changed attributes do not force an automatic failure in every case.
optionExplanations.B: Other attributes may still identify the element while confidence changes.
optionExplanations.C: A change does not guarantee increased stability.
optionExplanations.D: A changed target is not automatically skipped.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must be done first before you can capture video in Testim for a bug scenario?

options.text: Ensure the video capture feature is enabled in the Testim settings.
Add a validation step to the test case.
Install the Testim browser extension for Chrome.
Create a bug report template in the Testim dashboard.

practiceQuiz.hint: The capture/video functionality lives inside the extension, not the web editor.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Capture Video & Bug Scenario is a feature of the Testim Chrome Extension, so installing that extension is the required first step — it isn't a setting toggle, a validation step, or a bug report template, which are separate concerns that come after the extension is in place.

optionExplanations.A: Capture requires the extension, not just a setting.
optionExplanations.B: A validation step does not install video capture.
optionExplanations.C: The Chrome extension provides the described capture feature.
optionExplanations.D: A bug template does not replace the extension prerequisite.

quickRecap.value: Draft, Active, Evaluating, Quarantine — not 'Failed' or 'Archived'.
Single-location vs. multi-tag, searchable via label:<name>.
Advanced filters surface hidden steps (and filter by Groups/Actions/Validations/Wait for).
Saving a changed test creates a revision; restoring shared content can affect other instances.
Before/main/after phases and run configuration; invoke via a configured supported runner.
Group into collections + control run order (guaranteed only without --parallel).
Eligible master runs can attempt improvement below 70%; branch/settings/manual edits restrict eligibility.
Changed attributes → test may still pass, but confidence can drop.
Capture Video & Bug Scenario requires the Testim Chrome Extension installed first.
